title: Hard-wired input scan
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input, let $w$, $pre$, and $rest$ be Boolean lists, let $z$ be a Boolean list, and let $e$ be an eleven-register configuration record. If $w = pre \, ++ \, (z \, ++ \, rest)$, then for every prior output list $o$, the counter program for $M$, started at label $rZ$, with registers given by $e$, input position $|pre|$, and output $o$, reaches label $rZ$ with the register record obtained from $e$ by increasing its hard-wired-bit count by $|z|$, input position $|pre|+|z|$, and output $o$ followed by the concatenation, for each bit $b$ of $z$ in order, of the code consisting of a true bit followed by the encoding of the constant gate for $b$. The run takes at most $|z|(L_{�max}(M)+3)$ steps.
